author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose missing particles and per-pixel alpha effects
summary: Use a repeatable smoke, sparks, rain, or energy effect to separate missing draws from incorrect per-pixel alpha blending, compare software and hardware paths, and retain the least expensive correction that preserves layer order.
heroAlt: Official PCSX2 corrected hardware-rendering comparison with restored game geometry and effects

blocks.text: Determine whether particles are absent or composited incorrectly

A particle system can draw geometry that is present but fully transparent, use the wrong alpha test, appear behind an opaque surface, or vanish because a manual draw rule discards it. Select an effect that can be triggered on demand and has a known lifetime: a weapon spark, exhaust plume, rainfall burst, spell trail, or smoke cloud. Record its spawn point, duration, background color, and camera position.
Do not increase blending accuracy and skip-draw together. One can restore composition while the other deletes draws, leaving no defensible explanation for the result.

items: An in-game save immediately before a repeatable particle event.
A direct recording from spawn through disappearance.
Native resolution, system driver, and manual GS fixes reset.
A software-rendered correctness capture where practical.
Performance counters from the most particle-heavy portion.

blocks.text: Trace draw presence before blend accuracy

items: 1. Cold-boot and trigger the effect on the baseline hardware API at native resolution.
2. Inspect individual frames for faint geometry, solid rectangles, wrong color, reversed order, or complete absence.
3. Close the session and repeat on the other supported hardware API with identical settings.
4. Use software rendering briefly to record the intended count, opacity curve, and order against foreground objects.
5. Return to the more stable hardware path and raise blending accuracy one tier when draws exist but composition differs.
6. If particles remain completely absent, restore blending and remove broad skip-draw or discard rules before retesting.
7. Verify a second alpha feature such as foliage, shadows, fog, or a translucent HUD overlay.
8. Warm the device and replay the peak effect to measure the actual sustained cost.

blocks.text: Per-pixel alpha blending can require the emulator to reproduce operations the host hardware blend unit cannot express directly. Software-assisted paths improve accuracy but may add synchronization and cost. A spawn-to-fade recording shows whether particle count, opacity, and order are correct rather than treating any visible blob as success.
The accepted correction must preserve the full lifetime and surrounding layers.

items: The expected particles appear at the correct spawn point and time.
Opacity changes smoothly instead of switching between invisible and solid.
Foreground geometry occludes particles correctly while background remains visible through them.
The second alpha feature does not regress.
Sustained effects remain within the title's playable frame-time budget.

blocks.text: Alpha evidence that needs a different diagnosis

items: Software output is also empty: confirm game state, image integrity, and original behavior.
Particles appear only after an emulator state load: reproduce from an in-game save.
A blending tier restores smoke but removes foliage: reject the combined profile and isolate the title behavior.
Only a custom GPU driver fails: restore the system driver and report that driver separately.

blocks.text: Remove blending and draw-rule experiments separately

Restore Automatic blending first, confirm the recorded baseline, then remove any temporary skip-draw or alpha-test override. Cold-boot the spawn checkpoint after each rollback so the responsible variable remains identifiable.
Video compression can erase small particles
Thin rain, sparks, and translucent smoke are easily lost to low-bitrate encoding. Use local direct captures for QA and avoid judging particle count from a recompressed social or streaming preview.
